title: Free Printable Party Games: Bingo, Hunts, Word Puzzles
metaDescription: Free printable party games for birthdays, graduations, reunions and movie nights: bingo, scavenger hunts and word puzzles you can edit and print in minutes.
h1: Party Games (Free Printables for Any Celebration)
intro: Not every party has a theme or a professional host. These printable party games work for birthdays, graduations, reunions, retirements and movie nights, and they ask very little of the person running them.

sections.heading: Matching the game to the party
body: **Birthday party bingo** keeps a group of children occupied while the cake is being prepared. Stick to simple words like balloon, candle and present, and have the birthday child call the squares.
**Graduation and retirement bingo** works for mixed ages. Guests tick off moments in the speeches, such as a thank you to parents or a funny story, and everyone listens harder.
A **family reunion** is the best place for the icebreaker. The 'find someone who' sheet gets cousins who have not met to introduce themselves.
The **toddler scavenger hunt** and **indoor hunt** pages are made for children's parties when rain ruins the garden plan.

sections.heading: Setting up in a few minutes
body: Choose one game, edit the list, and print the sheets. If you will have more than twenty guests, make a few spare cards and keep a basket of pencils nearby. The [bingo card generator](/bingo-card-generator/) can make unique cards for every guest, and the [scavenger hunt generator](/scavenger-hunt-generator/) can print a team version.
Place a game on each table as a centerpiece. It gives quiet guests something easy to join, and it saves the host from being the only entertainer.
Small, silly prizes work best: a sticker, a candy bar, or the right to choose the next song.
Ask a teenager or an older cousin to be the caller. They enjoy the job, and it frees the host to cut the cake and pour drinks.

faq.q: What is the easiest party game to run?
faq.a: Bingo. Print the cards, call out the words and let guests mark them. No setup is needed beyond pencils.

faq.q: How many games do I need for a party?
faq.a: One or two is usually plenty. Many people only want a short activity between the food and the cake.
